column `composition` (element fractions as a compact formula string) and
column `target` (the measured critical temperature Tc (K)).

turns.answer_text:
From the training data, the compositions closest to very high Tc are overwhelmingly Cu–O cuprates with alkaline-earth/rare-earth cations. The low-to-mid Y/Ba/Cu/O entries are strongly depressed by oxygen deficiency or Zn/Pr substitutions, while the highest-Tc entries are clean layered cuprates. To target ~90 K rather than the 110–132 K Bi/Tl/Hg cuprates, I would choose a near-optimally oxygenated Y–Ba–Cu–O composition, approximately YBa₂Cu₃O₆.₉, with no Zn/Pr/Ni/Fe impurities.

Normalized elemental fractions for YBa₂Cu₃O₆.₉ are total atoms = 1 + 2 + 3 + 6.9 = 12.9.
